title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction: Context: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, order-theoretic 'Algèbre des figures' as a foundation for a tame, stratified 'analysis situs'. This is the programme of 'topologie modérée' sketched in Esquisse d'un programme. F is the set of 'figures'. It carries three order relations: ≤ (sub-figure), ≪ (refinement) and ≼ (subdivision). It has two distinguished subsets: M, whose elements are strata (sub-figures that are elements of M), and L, the 'lieux', the elementary pieces. ouvt(F) denotes the set of lieux constituting a figure F, related to its 'open' part or open sheaf. The page finishes the definitions begun on p.7. (1) F and G are compatible iff {F,G} is bounded above for ≤, i.e. both are sub-figures of a common figure. (2) F and G are disjoint iff they are compatible and their infimum in F is φ_F, the least element (the empty figure). Hence disjoint ⇒ compatible. (1.13) states that, by the axioms (not visible here), F and G are disjoint iff two conditions hold: ouvt(F) ∩ ouvt(G) = ∅ (no common lieu), and every element of ouvt(F) is compatible with every element of ouvt(G). Equivalently, every lieu of one is disjoint, in the order-theoretic sense, from every lieu of the other. So disjointness of figures is detected on lieux. Grothendieck concludes that compatibility and disjunction are significant structures when restricted to the subsets M and L. In the 'ensembliste' (set-theoretic) model they are trivial on L: any two lieux are compatible, and they are disjoint iff distinct, as for the pieces of a partition. Even in the set-theoretic tame case, however, compatibility on M is a genuinely extra structure. The next page claims that the atlas can be recovered up to unique isomorphism from (M, ≤, ≪, compatibility), or perhaps disjunction. It then proposes the notations F ∥ G for disjunction and F ◇ G for compatibility.
errors: No outright error. (1.13) is asserted 'par les axiomes', but the axioms are not on this page, so the equivalence cannot be checked here. The direction ⇐ in particular needs an axiom saying a figure is determined by, or generated by, its lieux, and that compatibility of the generating lieux gives compatibility of the figures.

There is a slight wording inconsistency between the right-hand formulation and its gloss. The bracket demands that elements of ouvt(F) and ouvt(G) be 'compatible'. The gloss says every lieu of one is 'disjoint' from every lieu of the other. These agree only given the empty intersection plus an axiom that distinct compatible lieux have infimum φ.

ideas.what: Compatibility of two figures defined as being bounded above in the sub-figure order; disjointness as compatible with infimum equal to the bottom element
ideas.modern_name: Consistency/coherence in a bounded-complete poset (Scott domains, coherence spaces); orthogonality in a poset with 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scott (domains, ~1970s), Girard (coherence spaces, 1987); classical lattice theory

ideas.what: Characterisation of disjointness of figures via their constituent lieux (no common lieu, and pairwise compatibility/disjointness of lieux)
ideas.modern_name: Locality of the disjointness relation in a stratified or cell-like structure (disjoint unions of strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in stratification theory and o-minimal geometry (cell decompositions)

ideas.what: Observation that, beyond the order relations, the compatibility relation on strata M is essential data, sufficient with ≤ and ≪ to reconstruct the atlas (stated on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial reconstruction of stratified spaces from posets of strata with extra relations (cf. face posets of regular CW complexes, exit-path/stratified homotopy data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Face-poset reconstruction: Björner and others (regular CW complexes); stratified spaces: Whitney, Thom, Mather, later MacPherson/Lurie for exit paths
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures, but not this order-theoretic formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'Algèbre des figures' is an attempt to axiomatise tame topology purely through order relations on figures (sub-figure, refinement, subdivision) plus compatibility and disjointness relations. It is a combinatorial/lattice-theoretic alternative to o-minimal structures. The page fixes the derived relations and their locality on lieux. The framework as a whole was never published or developed by others.
missed.quote: Ceci montre que les relations de compatibilité et de disjonction sont importantes aussi dans les ... ensembles M, L de F.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible bridge between tame geometry (o-minimality, Esquisse's 'topologie modérée') and order-theoretic or domain-theoretic semantics. However, this page alone contains only definitions and a routine lemma.

deep.surprise_reason: Definitional page inside an unpublished axiomatic programme. The content (compatibility = bounded above, disjoint = compatible with infimum ⊥, a locality lemma) is elementary. Interest lies only in its place within the unknown 'Algèbre des figures' project.
transcription_corrections: 'importantes aussi dans les [-cas di-]{+...+} — ensembles M, L de F': probably reads '...dans les sous-ensembles M, L de F' (the dash is a line-break continuation).

'Dans le cas des relations ensemblistes': the word before 'ensemblistes' is unclear in the image. It may be 'atlas' ('cas des atlas ensemblistes'), consistent with the next page's mention of 'l'atlas'.
'deux lieux sont toujours[?] compatibles': 'toujours' appears correct, with 'compatibles' written above a struck-out 'disjoints'.
'même dans le cas ensembliste et = modéré': likely 'ensembliste et modéré' (or '= modéré' meaning 'i.e. tame').
In (1.13), the struck-out first line contains 'tout' and 'ouvt(F) ∩ ouvt(G)'. The retained statement is 'ouvt(F) et ouvt(G) sont "disjoints" au sens suivant'.
